description_full: Weatherford International Corp provides equipment and services for the drilling, evaluation, completion, production, and intervention of oil, geothermal, and natural gas wells worldwide. It offers managed pressure drilling; directional drilling, and logging and measurement; services related to rotary-steerable systems, high temperature and high pressure sensors, drilling reamers, and circulation subs; open-hole and cased-hole logging services; wireline and drilling fluids; and intervention and remediation services. The company also provides tubular handling, management, and connection services; cementing products, including plugs, float and stage equipment, and torque-and-drag reduction technology for zonal isolation; completion tools, such as safety valves, production packers, downhole reservoir monitoring, flow control, isolation packers, multistage fracturing systems and sand-control technologies; liner hangers to suspend a casing string in high-temperature and high-pressure wells; and well services. In addition, it offers re-entry, fishing, and well abandonment services, as well as patented downhole tools, tubular-handling equipment, pressure-control equipment, and drill pipe and tubulars; artificial lift systems, including reciprocating rod, progressing cavity pumping, and related automation and control systems, as well as gas, hydraulic, plunger, and hybrid lift systems, as well as related automation and control systems; and software, automation and flow measurement solutions. Further, it provides electrical and hydraulic power transmission to subsea equipment; and pressure pumping and reservoir stimulation services, such as acidizing, fracturing, cementing, and coiled-tubing intervention. Weatherford International Corp was formerly known as Weatherford International plc and changed its name to Weatherford International Corp in November 2026. The company was incorporated in 1972 and is based in Houston, Texas.

financial_summary: Weatherford International Corp is a mid-cap energy business with a $5.8B market cap on $4.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years and -6% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at 30% against a 9% cost of capital — a 21-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 18% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $450M in free cash flow — roughly 9 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.57× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.5× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 6.0×.
Shareholder yield of 3.0% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 2.1% of the shares.
